extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks, consisting of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) tailored to evaluating logical reasoning, algebraic reasoning, and scientific reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were initially designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates, selecting examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, and discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process resulted in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%, with only 6 disagreements among the newly collected 736 questions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The creators are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise based on community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: There may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Annotations lack a unified format and structure due to the heterogeneity of the sources.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Model development validation and standard evaluation.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: To ensure consistency in annotation, we employed a two-step process. Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers... rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Specifically, among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in the annotated answers.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: we are committed to maintaining the datasets, such as refining the potential data noise, in response to the community feedback. Also, we are committed to evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: One limitation is the dataset coverage. While M ATHVISTA encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals... Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples (Table 1) having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: testmini contains 1,000 examples, intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources. The testset features the remaining 5,141 examples for standard evaluation.
